items.summary:
## Abstract

This chapter argues that transitioning fashion from a linear model to a regenerative system requires fundamental reform in design and manufacturing processes across the value chain. Analysis identifies critical impact hotspots—especially in wet processing—driven by intensive energy, water, and chemical use, with additional pressure from yield losses, resource sourcing, logistics, and waste generation. Key priorities include efficiency improvements, heat electrification, the adoption of renewable energy, and the targeted deployment of low-carbon steam systems. Material strategies emphasize recycled synthetics, next-generation cellulosics, bast fibers, and bio-based polymers that employ safe chemistries. Innovative manufacturing technologies—such as digital twins, artificial intelligence-enabled quality control, and on-demand microfactories—reduce waste and align production with actual demand, thereby optimizing resource utilization. Digital product passports enable traceability, facilitate disassembly, and promote responsible end-of-use pathways. Social regeneration—through living wages, safe workplaces, and resilient communities—is presented as indispensable to system transformation. Collectively, these actions represent Industry 5.0 in practice: human-centric, resilient, and sustainable. The chapter concludes that through heat decarbonization, data-driven operations, circular business models, and people-first governance, the fashion industry can transition from a net-negative to a net-positive force for climate, ecosystems, and society.

items.summary:
Circ® and H&M Group Advance Circular Fashion through UNIDO-Led SWITCH2CE Program

14 October 2025

DANVILLE, 14 October 2025 - Circ®, the only textile-to-textile recycler capable of taking polycotton blends and fully recovering both the polyester and the cellulose for reuse, today announced a collaboration with H&M Group, building on groundwork laid through the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO)-led SWITCH2CE program. For the first time, H&M will incorporate Circ’s recycled fibers from polycotton textile waste into its product offerings. The first products debut in Fall 2025, with a womenswear v-neck fleece sweatshirt made with Circ® Polyester and expands in Spring 2026 with menswear denim crafted with TENCEL™ | Circ® with REFIBRA™ Technology.

The Lenzing Group, a leading producer of wood-based specialty fibers, plays a central role in this partnership. For the first time, Circ’s recycled pulp will be commercialized through Lenzing’s global supply chain in the form of TENCEL™ | Circ® with REFIBRA™ Technology. Lenzing’s REFIBRA™ technology uses textile waste as a raw material, in addition to wood sources from certified or controlled origins, giving waste a new life. Within this partnership the Lyocell fiber branded under TENCEL™ I Circ® with REFIBRA™ technology is crafted with 30% Circ pulp from recycled textile waste. This milestone showcases how existing fiber platforms can be leveraged to unlock circularity at scale.

This global launch builds on the global SWITCH2CE program led by the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), and a two-year pilot with Intellecap, and H&M Group, through which Circ piloted its recycling technology with H&M Group’s suppliers in Bangladesh, successfully recycling 2.6 tonnes of polycotton waste into Circ® Lyocell and Circ® Polyester. Circ was selected for its blended fiber recycling capabilities as well as its commitment to continuously assess and optimize their process to reduce environmental impact as they scale. The project proved the commercial viability of Circ’s platform within local supply chains and laid the groundwork for this global launch.

"Collaborating with key partners on projects like this is essential to our vision: to grow our business decoupled from resource use and extraction, with products and materials circulating at their highest value” said Cecilia Strömblad Brännsten, Head of Resource Use and Circularity at H&M Group.

“True circularity will require the entire value chain to work together. By integrating Circ’s recycled pulp into our TENCEL™ Refibra technology and partnering with H&M Group, we’ve demonstrated how existing mill relationships and fiber platforms can be leveraged to make circular fashion commercially viable,” said Florian Heubrander, Executive Vice President Commercial Textiles at Lenzing Group.

“H&M Group brings global fashion scale, and Lenzing brings decades of fiber expertise. Together they provide the infrastructure needed to make circular fashion commercially viable,” said Peter Majeranowski, CEO at Circ. “By working with partners of this caliber, we’re showing how fiber producers and global brands can close the loop at commercial volumes. This builds on our work through the UNIDO SWITCH2CE program with H&M Group, which proved our technology could recycle blended textile waste within local supply chains. What we’re announcing today is the next step of turning pilots into global practice.”

“Through pilot projects like our collaboration with H&M Group and textile suppliers in Bangladesh, UNIDO helps de-risk investments in innovation that strengthen competitiveness and resilience. By advancing a circular value chain approach through public-private partnerships, we are accelerating climate-smart solutions that can be scaled for lasting impact.” said Mark Draeck, SWITCH2CE Chief Technical Advisor at UNIDO.

The upcoming products have been developed through collaboration across the supply chain. For the menswear denim, recycled lyocell from Circ was woven into fabric by AGI Denim. For the womenswear fleece sweatshirt, Circ recycled PET chip was converted into polyester staple fiber by Palmetto and then knitted into fabric by Fakir Knitwear. Circ’s technology is designed to fit smoothly into existing manufacturing, allowing partners to adopt circular materials without disruption. Through initiatives such as Circ®-Ready, Circ works with supply chain partners to make circular fashion possible at scale.

Garment samples from this collaboration will be on display at The Textile Exchange Conference 2025 in Lisbon, Portugal, October 13–17, 2025.

About UNIDO

The United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) is the UN’s specialized agency that promotes inclusive and sustainable industrial development. UNIDO supports sustainable supply chains, combats climate breakdown through renewable energy and efficiency, and strengthens agribusinesses to end hunger....

items.summary:
UNIDO-led circular textile pilot delivers second commercial product

07 October 2026

Dhaka, Bangladesh, 07 October 2026 – The SWITCH to Circular Economy Value Chains (SWITCH2CE) project led by the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) has reached another important milestone, with a second commercially available H&M product made from recycled fibres originating from the project now available to consumers. The achievement demonstrates how textile waste can be transformed into market-ready fashion and scaled by industry actors.Menswear denim made with recycled fibres that trace back to the SWITCH2CE pilot in Bangladesh is now available in H&M's online store in selected markets. The Straight Regular Jeans contain TENCEL™ Limited Edition Lyocell fibres produced with 30% Circ® pulp recycled from textile waste.

The launch builds on the pilot's first commercial success, a womenswear fleece sweatshirt made with Circ® Polyester, introduced in Fall 2025 as part of the first commercial sourcing partnership between H&M Group and Circ®.

Both products trace their origins to 2.6 tonnes of blended cotton-polyester production waste collected by Fakir Knitwear, a Bangladesh-based garment manufacturer participating in the SWITCH2CE pilot. Instead of becoming waste, the blended polycotton production offcuts were collected and separated into two recycled material streams before being processed into Circ® Lyocell, made from the recovered cotton component, and Circ® Polyester, produced from the recovered polyester.

While the recycled polyester was knitted by Fakir Knitwear into fleece fabric for the womenswear sweatshirt launched by H&M in Fall 2025, the recycled cotton pulp was converted by Lenzing Group into TENCEL™ Limited Edition Lyocell fibres containing 30% recycled content. Almost a tonne of these fibres was used to manufacture the final menswear jeans now available through H&M.

The launch reflects collaboration across global and local partners. UNIDO led the pilot under the SWITCH2CE programme, co-funded by the European Union and the Government of Finland. Circ® provided recycling technology and Lenzing Group contributed its fibre expertise. Manufacturing partners in South Asia, part of H&M’s global supply chain, anchored the production activities, with Palmetto converting recycled PET chip into polyester staple fibre for the fleece track. H&M Group brought the products to market.

Beyond delivering commercial products, the pilot demonstrates that circular textiles can represent a viable business opportunity. It shows that blended textile waste generated in Bangladesh can be sorted, recycled and transformed into high-value garments for the market.

While some recycling processes currently take place outside Bangladesh because of technological limitations, the long-term ambition is to build these capabilities domestically. SWITCH2CE is therefore supporting a chemical recycling readiness study alongside broader ecosystem initiatives that will inform Bangladesh's national circular textile strategy. Together, these efforts aim to establish a formalized feedstock supply chain and enable textile-to-textile recycling at scale, allowing more of the value created from the country's textile waste to be retained domestically.
